questions.q: Why is one-time testing at go-live insufficient for an Oracle Fusion Cloud implementation?
options: Because Oracle never updates Fusion Cloud again after go-live
Because Oracle applies mandatory quarterly updates that can change standard functionality or default behavior
Because UAT sign-off is only valid for 30 days
Because the configuration workbook expires after go-live
questions.explain: Oracle applies quarterly updates to every environment on a fixed schedule, and any update can change functionality or defaults a company's configuration depends on, so testing must continue after go-live.

questions.q: What does a regression test suite typically contain?
options: A curated, smaller subset of scripts covering critical processes and anything a specific update flags as changed
Every test script ever written for the project, including all of UAT
Only defect log entries from the original SIT cycle
The original project charter and scope statement
questions.explain: A regression suite is a curated, smaller set of critical scripts plus items flagged by the update's readiness documentation — not a full UAT re-run.

questions.q: When is the regression test suite typically re-run relative to a quarterly update?
options: After the update reaches Production, to see what broke
Exactly one year after go-live
Only once, during the original implementation
In the Test environment, during the window after Test is updated but before Production is updated
questions.explain: The regression suite is re-run in Test during the two-week window between the Test update and the matching Production update, catching issues before they reach Production.

questions.q: What does Oracle's update "readiness documentation" help a team decide?
options: Which Executive Sponsor to assign
What's changed in the update and which optional new features to opt into
How to write the original Business Requirements Document
The legal entity structure for Phase 2
questions.explain: Readiness documentation describes what's new or changed in an update, helping teams decide what to regression test and which opt-in features to enable.

questions.q: What did Brightfield's consultant find in the readiness notes for its first post-go-live update?
options: A new legal entity requirement
A new Executive Sponsor assignment
A changed default in automatic reconciliation matching behavior
A requirement to rebuild the entire configuration workbook
questions.explain: The consultant spotted a changed default in automatic reconciliation matching behavior and added that scenario to the regression suite before the update reached Production.
